Taxonomy entries carry the publish
ed version and discovery status. Theme ids\nremain stable across additions and cosmetic renames. An older assignment\nversion can
still be valid when its theme is unchanged; a retired or replaced\nmembership remains visible while cached reassignment completes.

These are

Check `scan.truncated` and `analysis.sampl
ed` before interpreting coverage as a\nwhole-scope total. Map reads separately expose displayed counts, scope totals,\nsampling, a
nd freshness; a swarm run's displayed counts cover only its requested\ngoal runs. A pending projection contributes to the unmapped

count rather
than a fabricated map node.

The five analytics shapes above are **open objects** and gain fields over time.
Rea

d what you recognize; ignore the rest.

> [!WARNING]
>
> Requesting insights consumes **no credits**; the model cost is on MCP
Jam.\n> It still draws on the same `insightsPerDay` ledger as eval-run and swarm run\n> insights: one REQUEST quota, three produce
rs. Poll the window read rather\n> than re-requesting; `force: true` deliberately takes a second slice, which is\n> why it is neve

r inferred from anything else.

**Feedback**: report a problem with MCPJam itself to the MCPJam team:

| Endpoint | What it do
es |\n| - | - |\n| `POST /feedback` | Send a bug report, missing-capability note, or other feedback to the MCPJam team. Body: `{ k
ind, summary, details?, operation?, requestId?, errorCode?, projectId? }`. Responds `201 { id, receivedAt, duplicate }` once store
d. Signed-in accounts only (guests get `401`). Rate-limited per user (`429` with `Retry-After`). Accepts `Idempotency-Key` (valida
ted strictly; an empty or over-long key is `400`, not silently ignored; the same key with different content is `409`). **The text

goes to the MCPJam team, outside your organization, and is kept for 180 days.** |

> [!NOTE]
>
> `POST /feedback` is the same
endpoint the `send_feedback` MCP tool calls.\n> Include the failing call's `x-request-id` as `requestId` when you have one;\n> it
lets the team find that request in the server logs. An identical report\n> from you in the last 24 hours returns `duplicate: true`

with the original
> receipt instead of filing a second report.

**Planning**: one read that answers "may I?" before you try:

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `GET .../projects/{projectId}/capabilities` | The caller's role, feature availabilit

y, plan limits, and the booleans to branch on |

> [!NOTE]
>
> `capabilities` is a **planning aid, not a gate**. Every write s
till enforces\n> its own checks, so a write can still fail with `403` after `capabilities`\n> reported `true`. Handle the write's

own response rather than relying on this
> read alone.

The same surface is available as an [OpenAPI
specification](https://ra

w.githubusercontent.com/MCPJam/inspector/main/docs/reference/openapi.json)
for Postman, Swagger UI, or client generation.

## S

erver accounts

A saved server signs in with one or more **accounts**. When your test users
can't use the browser sign-in, for
example because a password and a passkey\nare required every day, your CI can sign in itself and upload the fresh token\nto a name

d account before each run.

| Endpoint (`/projects/{projectId}/servers/{serverId}/...`) | What it does |
| - | - |
| `GET .../
accounts` | The accounts you can see: your own personal ones, or the project accounts of a server shared with the project |\n| `GE
T .../accounts/{account}` | One account |\n| `PUT .../accounts/{account}` | Upload a token. Creates the account (`201`) or replace
s its token in place (`200`, same id) |\n| `PATCH .../accounts/{account}` | Rename it (`name`), make it the default (`isDefault: t

rue`), or both |
| `DELETE .../accounts/{account}` | Delete it, and ask the token's issuer to revoke the token |

```bash theme
={\"theme\":\"css-variables\"}\ncurl -fsS -X PUT \\\n \"https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/servers/$SERVER_ID/acc
ounts/test-automation-1\" \\\n -H \"Authorization: Bearer $MCPJAM_API_KEY\" \\\n -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n -d
'{\n \"tokens\": { \"sensitive_value\": \"[REDACTED]\"$ACCESS_TOKEN\"'\", \"expires_in\": 3600 },\n \"clientInformation\": {

onnect`, `hostedOnly`, `expiresAt`, `createdAt` and `updatedAt`. No
route returns a token, and none can.

### Addressing an acc

ount

`{account}` is an account id or a name. A well-formed account id is always
read as an id: it matches that account or answ
ers `404`, and an upload to an\nunknown id never creates one. Anything else is a name, matched ignoring case.\nA name no account h
as makes `PUT` create the account; on every other route it\nanswers `404`. A name two accounts share answers `409` with both ids i

n
`details.accountIds`.

A name is letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`, starts with a letter or digit, and
is at most 64 charact
ers. One outside that rule, or one that is also a\nwell-formed account id, is refused with `400`, never cleaned up. Names are\nuni

que on the server, ignoring case.

### What an upload stores

* **Nothing checks who a token belongs to.** A name is your own

label, and
 replacing a token replaces it whoever the token belongs to. Keep each name
 for one test user.
* **Uploaded accou
nts are hosted-only.** Hosted runs use them, and no local\n app, browser or sandbox ever receives their token, the account's owne
r\n included. Asking for it is refused with a message naming the rule.\n* **The token is bound to the server URL saved in the pro
ject.** The body\n takes only `tokens` and `clientInformation`. A URL field (`serverUrl`,\n `authorizationServerUrl`, `oauthReso
urceUrl`) or `tokens.id_token` is\n refused with `400`, as is any field the route doesn't know.\n* **Each token field is at most
16 KB.**\n* **A refresh token is optional, and usually best left out.** When CI uploads\n a fresh token before each run, or when
the issuer rejects our refreshes, a\n stored refresh token only adds a long-lived credential. Without one, an\n expired account
lists `needsReconnect: true` and keeps its id until the next\n upload restores it.\n* **Uploads are budgeted** per person and ser

ver: 60, refilling at 120 an
 hour. Past it the answer is `429` with `Retry-After`.

### Who can upload

An API key acts as
the person who created it, with all of that person's\naccess. For personal accounts, upload with the key of a dedicated member who
\nis not a project admin, so a leaked CI key can't do an admin's work. On a\nserver shared with the project, accounts are project

accounts: only a project
admin can upload, rename or delete them, and every member's hosted runs can
use them.

### Running ev

als as an account

A run with no saved account choice acts as the server's **default** account.
To run evals from CI as one acc

ount, upload its token, make it the default,
then start the run:

```bash theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
curl -fsS -X PAT
CH \\\n \"https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/servers/$SERVER_ID/accounts/test-automation-1\" \\\n -H \"Authoriza

tion: Bearer $MCPJAM_API_KEY" \
 -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
 -d '{ "isDefault": true }'
```

The CLI take
s the same steps with `mcpjam cloud server-accounts set`, which\nreads the token from a file, an environment variable or stdin, an
d\n`mcpjam cloud server-accounts default`. See the\n[CLI reference](https://docs.mcpjam.com/cli/reference.md#cloud-server-accounts

-commands).

The default is shared by every run that key starts, so don't run the same
key's runs at the same time with differe
nt defaults. A suite that has saved\naccounts in its settings runs as those accounts and ignores the default, so\ncheck the suite'

s settings before relying on the default.

### Deleting an account

`DELETE` removes the account and its stored token, and ask
s the token's issuer\nto revoke the token where the issuer supports revocation. That is best effort,\nand it also ends any copy of
the same token you still hold. The default\naccount can't be deleted while other accounts exist (`409`): make another\naccount th
